source_paper: Semantic Web in Healthcare: A Systematic Literature Review of Application, Research Gap, and Future Research Avenues
Claim: While the target paper categorizes Semantic Web (SW) applications in healthcare, it leaves open several critical gaps: 1) The lack of standardized evidence mapping and data consistency frameworks across heterogeneous medical sources; 2) Insufficient integration of SW with advanced AI/ML performance evaluation methodologies; 3) A lack of focus on the ethical, privacy, and regulatory implications of semantic data sharing; and 4) The scarcity of longitudinal studies assessing the practical translation of SW technologies into clinical workflows.
Warrant: Direction: Future research should focus on: 1) Developing unified evidence mapping databases to standardize clinical data reporting; 2) Integrating SW technologies with machine learning to create hybrid, explainable AI systems for healthcare; 3) Establishing robust ethical and governance frameworks for semantic data interoperability; and 4) Conducting long-term empirical evaluations of SW systems in active clinical environments.. Approach: Technical solutions include: 1) Designing neuro-symbolic AI architectures that combine semantic knowledge graphs (RDF/OWL) with deep learning models; 2) Implementing automated data curation pipelines using tools like OpenRefine and standardized medical ontologies (e.g., SNOMED-CT, UMLS) to ensure data consistency; 3) Integrating decentralized privacy-preserving technologies, such as blockchain or federated learning, with semantic webs to secure patient data; and 4) Developing standardized benchmarking suites to evaluate the performance and scalability of semantic queries in real-time healthcare systems.
